applicationPortal.value: Graduate music admission is a two-part process requiring separate applications to The University of Texas at Austin and to the Sarah and Ernest Butler School of Music. The Butler School accepts applications for fall semesters only. Applicants must submit the university application before beginning the Butler School of Music application. For Piano, the page lists MM in Performance and MM Literature & Pedagogy. The University Application includes the graduate application and application fee, three letters of recommendation written within the last twelve months, official transcripts from every senior college attended, and test scores if required. The program does not require a GRE score. The Butler School of Music application includes an introductory video of one to three minutes, statement of purpose of about 500 words, resume or curriculum vitae, repertoire list, prescreening materials, audition-date selection, and teacher preferences.

applicationFee.value: Application portal: UT Austin Graduate School application followed by the Butler School of Music application. Application fee: $65 for U.S. Graduate applicants. auditionRequirements.value: Piano applicants must submit prescreening videos within the Butler School of Music application by December 1. Current Butler School students applying for a further degree and graduate students reapplying to end an official leave of absence are exempt from the prescreening requirement. Prescreening results are released in mid-December. Each required repertoire selection should be uploaded as a separate video file. Individual movements or excerpts should be uploaded as separate digital files. Video format is required, and audio-only submissions are not accepted. Recordings must be genuinely performed by the applicant, must not be edited, and must not include added effects such as reverb. Applicants must review recordings for distortion or excessive buzz, and accompaniment, if required, should not drown out the applicant's playing. Auditions take place at the Butler School of Music. Exceptions are made only for applicants who reside outside the continental United States; those applicants may choose to audition by video, and video auditions are due with the music application by the application deadline. After passing prescreening, the audition confirmation is posted in the music application portal in mid-December. Applicants should not make travel plans until the audition date is confirmed. The portal is updated with audition-day information one to two weeks before the scheduled date. Invited applicants should make themselves available for the entire audition day. Applicants who submitted the optional teaching sample video are scheduled for a 10-15 minute interview with Dr. Margarita Denenburg on the same day as the audition, covering teaching experience and interests, personal goals as pianist and educator, and approach to pedagogical principles and practices.

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening repertoire: The prescreening recording must include the performance of a solo recital-style program of at least 45 minutes of music. Prescreening repertoire: Applicants should select pieces that represent the highest level of their musicality and abilities. Prescreening repertoire: A minimum of three styles should be represented. Prescreening repertoire: The program must include all or part of a major work from the Classical period. Prescreening repertoire: Concertos and other non-solo works are not preferred or recommended. Prescreening repertoire: Optional for teaching assistantship consideration, students interested in applying for a teaching assistantship in piano must request an interview and submit a sample teaching video as part of the prescreening materials. Prescreening repertoire: The teaching video should be 10-20 minutes long, unedited, and show the applicant interacting with students in private instruction or classroom piano. Final audition repertoire: If invited, prepare 45 minutes of music. Final audition repertoire: The live audition duration will be shorter than 45 minutes. Additional repertoire notes: Applicants who have submitted the optional teaching sample video will be scheduled for a 10-15 minute interview with the piano pedagogy professor on the same day as the audition. Additional repertoire notes: Video auditions are permitted only for applicants residing outside the continental United States and are due with the music application by the application deadline.
